Stuffed Mushrooms

Tender mushroom caps filled with seasoned breadcrumbs, Pecorino Romano, garlic, parsley, and mint.

Recipe Notes Original Giada recipe; no Daniel changes recorded yet.
Appetizers & Snacks
Yield28 mushrooms
Prep10 min
Cook25 min
Method400°F
DifficultyEasy
Main IngredientMushrooms

Ingredients

Filling

Mushrooms

Cooking Stages

1

Prepare

Preheat the oven to 400°F. Clean the mushrooms and remove the stems.

2

Mix filling

Combine breadcrumbs, cheese, garlic, parsley, mint, salt, pepper, and 2 tablespoons oil. It should be moist but crumbly.

3

Fill

Oil a baking sheet. Spoon filling into the caps and drizzle lightly with the remaining oil.

4

Bake

Bake about 25 minutes, until the mushrooms are tender and the tops are lightly golden.

5

Rest

Let stand 5 minutes before serving warm.

Parmesan Pomodoro

A simple tomato sauce flavored with garlic, basil, carrot, and a Parmigiano-Reggiano rind.

Recipe Notes Foundation sauce. Personal changes not yet recorded.
Sauces & DipsComponents & BasicsPasta Sauces
Yield6 servings
Prep15 min
Cook50 min
MethodStovetop
DifficultyEasy
Main IngredientTomatoes

Ingredients

Sauce

To Finish

Cooking Stages

1

Start the sauce

Warm the oil over medium heat. Add garlic and cook until fragrant and lightly golden, not brown.

2

Simmer

Add tomatoes, basil, carrot, cheese rind, and salt. Simmer gently about 35 minutes until slightly thickened and the carrot is tender.

3

Finish the sauce

Remove the basil, carrot, and rind. Crush or blend the sauce to the texture you prefer.

4

Cook pasta

Boil pasta in salted water until just tender. Save some pasta water.

5

Combine

Move pasta into the sauce. Add cheese and butter, tossing until glossy. Loosen with pasta water if needed.

Prepare sauce

Main Dishes · Italian

Chicken Piccata

Thin chicken cutlets in a bright lemon, butter, broth, and caper sauce.

Recipe Notes No personal modifications recorded yet.
Main Dishes
Yield4 servings
Prep5 min
Cook15 min
MethodStovetop
DifficultyEasy
Main IngredientChicken

Ingredients

Chicken

Sauce

Cooking Stages

1

Prepare chicken

Season the chicken and coat lightly with flour. Shake off the extra.

2

Brown

Heat oil with half the butter over medium-high heat. Cook chicken about 3 minutes per side until golden. Transfer to a plate.

3

Build sauce

Add broth, lemon juice, and capers. Scrape the browned bits from the pan and simmer a few minutes.

4

Finish chicken

Return chicken to the pan briefly to heat through. Transfer to a serving plate.

5

Finish sauce

Whisk in remaining butter, spoon over chicken, and add parsley.

Options

Quick Broiler Method — About 17 Minutes

Season four 6-ounce chicken breasts with 1½ teaspoons kosher salt and rub with 1 teaspoon olive oil. Place in an oven-safe skillet with 1 teaspoon lemon zest, 2 tablespoons lemon juice, ⅔ cup low-sodium chicken broth, and 2 tablespoons capers. Broil 10–12 minutes until browned and cooked through. Rest the chicken while the pan sauce simmers on the stovetop; whisk in 2 tablespoons room-temperature butter and 2 tablespoons chopped parsley.

Source: Giadzy Easy Chicken Piccata.

Prep30 min
Cook120 min

DifficultyModerate
Main IngredientBeef & Pasta

Ingredients

Bolognese

Ricotta Layer

Assembly

Cooking Stages

1

Build the Bolognese

Brown beef in olive oil, then add carrot, onion, garlic, tomato paste, and red wine. Add tomatoes, water, and Parmesan rind; simmer about 30 minutes.

2

Mix ricotta layer

Combine ricotta, salt, drained spinach, and basil.

3

Heat oven to 400°F. Butter a 9×13-inch dish. Layer sauce, noodles, ricotta mixture, mozzarella, and Parmesan, repeating to make three noodle layers.

Bake and rest

Cover with buttered foil and bake 20 minutes. Uncover and bake 20 minutes more. Rest 15 minutes before slicing.

Ricotta Gnocchi

Soft ricotta dumplings that cook quickly and pair well with butter or tomato sauce.

Recipe Notes Keep the dough soft; too much flour makes the gnocchi heavy.
Main DishesPasta & Gnocchi
Yield4 servings
Prep25 min
Cook10 min
MethodStovetop
DifficultyModerate
Main IngredientPasta

Ingredients

Gnocchi

Cooking Stages

1

Drain ricotta

Remove excess moisture so the dough does not need too much flour.

2

Mix dough

Combine ricotta, egg, Parmesan, salt, and most of the flour. Mix only until it holds together.

3

Shape

Divide and roll into ropes on a floured surface. Cut into bite-size pieces.

4

Boil

Cook in salted boiling water until they float, then continue 1–2 minutes.

5

Sauce

Move directly into warm butter or tomato sauce and serve.

Ingredients

Pomodoro

1

Simmer the sauce

Combine tomatoes, carrot, onion, basil stems, Parmesan rind, and olive oil. Simmer gently for 40–45 minutes until slightly reduced; season with salt, then remove the vegetables, herbs, and rind.

Stir gnocchi and ½ cup Parmesan into the sauce. Transfer to the dish and top with mozzarella and remaining Parmesan.

Bake

Bake 25–30 minutes, until bubbling and browned on top. Rest 10 minutes before serving.

Yield2 servings
Prep20 min
Cook5 min
MethodStovetop
DifficultyModerate
Main IngredientPotatoes

Ingredients

Gnocchi

Cooking Stages

1

Cook and rice potatoes

Pierce potatoes and microwave until tender, about 12 minutes. Split, let steam escape, then rice the warm flesh.

2

Make dough

Add salt, pepper, and flour. Make a well, add beaten egg, and mix gently. Knead only 4–5 times.

Shape

Divide into four pieces, roll into ½-inch ropes, cut into 1-inch pieces, and roll over a gnocchi board or fork for ridges.

4

Cook

Boil in generously salted water until the gnocchi float and are tender; remove with a slotted spoon and sauce immediately.

Appetizers & Snacks · Florida

Daniel’s Florida-Style Smoked Fish Dip

A smoky, fish-forward dip that uses only enough dairy to hold everything together.

Family Favorite Daniel’s guiding principle: fish over cream. BBQ rub removed from the cure.
Appetizers & SnacksFamily Favorites
Yield10–16 servings
Prep30 min
Cook1½–3 hr
Method225°F
DifficultyEasy
Main IngredientFish

Ingredients

Fish

Cure

Dip Base

Cooking Stages

1

Cure fish

Pat fish dry, coat with the equal-parts seasoning, wrap tightly, and refrigerate 24 hours.

2

Rinse

Rinse under cold water and pat completely dry.

3

Air-dry

Refrigerate uncovered on a rack for 2–4 hours, until the outside feels dry and slightly sticky.

4

Smoke

Smoke at 225°F until the fish reaches 145°F, usually 1½–3 hours depending on thickness. Cool.

5

Prepare vegetables

Dice most onion and celery. Blend smaller portions, including celery tops.

6

Prepare fish

Remove skin and bones. Keep most fish in medium flakes; blend only darker, firmer smoked exterior pieces.

7

Combine

Mix dairy and Worcestershire, then gently fold in fish and vegetables. Add dairy only as needed.

8

Rest

Refrigerate overnight for the best flavor.

Sides · American

Fancy Mac and Cheese

A richer, more elevated mac and cheese made with shell pasta, a bold cheese blend, mustard powder, and Worcestershire, without a hard baked crust.

Daniel’s Fancy Version This was the successful richer version. Daniel used shells, mustard powder instead of Dijon, Worcestershire sauce, strong cheeses, and no paprika.
SidesPasta & Gnocchi
Yield8 servings
Prep25 min
Cook35 min
Method350°F
DifficultyModerate
Main IngredientCheese

Ingredients

Pasta

Cheese Sauce

For the Pan

Cooking Stages

1

Cook the Shells

Boil the shells in salted water until about 2 minutes short of fully tender. Drain well so they do not become soft during baking.

2

Start the Sauce

Melt the butter over medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 1–2 minutes, until smooth and lightly bubbling but not browned.

3

Add the Milk and Cream

Whisk in the milk and cream gradually. Cook until the sauce lightly coats the back of a spoon.

4

Add the Flavor

Lower the heat. Stir in mustard powder, Worcestershire, pepper, and most of the cheese. Mix until smooth. Taste before adding salt because the cheese and Worcestershire are already salty.

5

Combine

Fold the shells into the cheese sauce. The mixture should look slightly looser than the final result because it will thicken in the oven.

6

Heat Without Making a Crust

Transfer to a greased baking dish, add the remaining cheese, cover tightly with foil, and bake at 350°F until hot and creamy, about 20–25 minutes.

7

Make Ahead and Reheat

Cool, cover, and refrigerate. Reheat covered at 325–350°F until hot. Add a small splash of milk before reheating only if the pasta looks dry.

Scale This Recipe

Original8 servings
Scale ForServings
servings

Original recipe

Storage & Serving

My Notes

This was the richer “fancy” version and turned out very good.

  • Use shell pasta.
  • Use mustard powder instead of Dijon mustard.
  • Add Worcestershire sauce for stronger flavor.
  • Do not add paprika.
  • Keep the dish covered because Daniel does not want a hard baked crust.
  • This version is richer and more upscale than the everyday version.

Kitchen Guides · Kitchen Help

Knife Sharpening Guide

A simple reference for using a belt-style knife sharpener without removing more metal than necessary.

Daniel’s Future Reference Daniel previously used P500 and then P3000, alternating left and right for 10 strokes on sharpen and refine. Next time, use fewer passes and choose the coarse belt only when the edge actually needs it.
Kitchen Guides
TypeKitchen guide
Prep5 min
UseAs needed
MethodBelt sharpener
DifficultyCareful
TopicKnife Care

What You Need

What You Need

Belt Purpose

Guide

1

Check the edge first

Use the coarse belt only when the knife is truly dull or damaged. A knife that only needs touching up may need the fine belt alone.

2

Use light pressure

Let the belt do the work. Heavy pressure can remove too much metal and heat the edge.

3

Alternate sides

Make one smooth pass on the left, then one on the right. Keep the blade moving at the same speed and angle.

4

Use fewer passes

Start with a small number of alternating passes, then test. Do not automatically do 10 passes per side on every belt.

5

Refine the edge

After the edge is formed, switch to the fine belt and use only enough light alternating passes to smooth it.

6

Clean and test safely

Wipe the blade clean and test on paper or food. Never run a finger along the sharp edge.

Care & Safety

Unplug the sharpener before changing belts. Keep the blade cool, clean off metal dust, and store knives so the edge does not strike other utensils.

My Notes

Daniel previously used P500 and then P3000, alternating left and right for 10 strokes on sharpen and refine. Next time, use fewer passes and choose the coarse belt only when the edge actually needs it.

Guide History

Reference: Open source

Everyday Creamy Mac and Cheese

A familiar, full-flavored mac and cheese with shell pasta and a straightforward cheddar-based sauce—less fancy than Daniel’s richer version but still bold and creamy.

Daniel’s Everyday Version Designed to taste more familiar and less upscale than the fancy recipe while keeping the strong flavor Daniel prefers.
SidesPasta & Gnocchi
Yield8 servings
Prep15 min
Cook25 min
MethodStovetop
DifficultyEasy
Main IngredientCheese

Ingredients

Pasta

Cheese Sauce

Cooking Stages

1

Cook the Shells

Boil the shells in salted water until just tender. Drain and set aside.

2

Make the Base

Melt butter over medium heat. Stir in flour and cook for 1–2 minutes without browning.

3

Add the Milk

Whisk in the milk gradually. Cook until slightly thickened and smooth.

4

Add Seasoning and Cheese

Lower the heat. Stir in mustard powder, Worcestershire, garlic powder, onion powder, and cheese. Mix until smooth and creamy.

5

Combine and Serve

Fold in the shells. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve immediately while creamy.

Options

More familiar flavor: Use all sharp and mild cheddar.

Smoother melt: Use Monterey Jack for part of the cheese.

Make it stronger: Add Worcestershire a little at a time after tasting.

Keep it simple: Do not add paprika, specialty cheese, breadcrumbs, or a baked topping.

Finish in skillet

5

Serve

Serve warm.

Chicken Cordon Bleu

Thin chicken breasts rolled with prosciutto and Gruyère, coated in seasoned panko, and baked until golden.

Recipe NotesThe source uses prosciutto and Gruyère for a deeper savory flavor.
Main Dishes
Yield4 servings
Prep20 min
Cook25 min
Method350°F oven
DifficultyModerate
Main IngredientChicken

Ingredients

Chicken Rolls

Breading

Cooking Stages

1

Heat oven

Preheat oven to 350°F.

2

Flatten and fill

Pound chicken between plastic wrap to ¼-inch thickness. Cover each with prosciutto and Gruyère.

3

Roll

Tuck in sides, roll tightly using the plastic wrap, twist ends, and chill about 30 minutes so the rolls hold their shape.

4

Bread

Season flour, eggs, and panko. Add thyme, garlic, and melted butter to panko. Coat rolls in flour, egg, then panko.

5

Bake

Drizzle with olive oil and bake 20–25 minutes, until golden and the chicken reaches 165°F.

6

Serve

Rest briefly and slice into pinwheels.

Options

Easy Weeknight Method — About 15 Minutes

Mix 2 tablespoons mascarpone with 3 tablespoons whole-grain mustard. Pan-sear four 5-ounce chicken breasts in 2 tablespoons olive oil, about 4 minutes on the first side and 2 minutes after flipping. Top each with Swiss cheese, Black Forest ham, mascarpone-mustard sauce, and more Swiss. Broil about 2 minutes until melted and bubbly.

Source: Giadzy Easy Chicken Cordon Bleu.

Neapolitan Pizza

The pizza-class dough from Italy: a long-rise Neapolitan-style dough made with 00 or type 1 flour.

Recipe NotesOriginal source: Federica’s pizza class in Italy. Preserve the long-rise method.
Main DishesBreads & DoughsPizza
Yield4 pizzas
Prep20 min + 8–12 hr rise
CookDepends on oven
MethodHigh-heat pizza
DifficultyModerate
Main IngredientPizza

Ingredients

Dough

Cooking Stages

1

Mix dough

Add salt and yeast to the water, then add flour and knead until smooth and elastic.

2

First rise

Cover with a dry cloth and rise about 2 hours.

3

Divide

Divide into 4 dough balls.

4

Long rise

Let the dough balls rise another 6–10 hours. Use the same day or refrigerate and use the next day only.

5

Shape

Press from the center outward with your fingers. Do not use a rolling pin.

Fresh Pasta Dough

The professional Giadzy version is kept instead of the shorter handwritten pasta-dough note.

Professional SourceGiada De Laurentiis / Giadzy
Breads & DoughsComponents & BasicsPasta & Gnocchi
Yield4 servings
Prep15 min
Cook3–5 min
MethodPasta dough
DifficultyModerate
Main IngredientFlour & Eggs

Ingredients

Dough

Cooking Stages

1

Mix

Whisk the flours together and form a well. Add eggs, yolks, olive oil, and water, gradually pulling flour into the center.

2

Knead

Work the dough until it no longer sticks, then knead 8–10 minutes until smooth and pliable.

3

Rest

Wrap tightly and rest at least 30 minutes.

4

Roll and cut

Use a pasta machine or rolling pin to make thin sheets, then cut into the desired shape. Dust with flour to prevent sticking.

5

Cook

Boil fresh pasta in generously salted water, checking after 1 minute; most shapes are al dente within 3–4 minutes.

Breads & Doughs · Italian

Italian Bread

A simple two-rise Italian loaf with a crisp golden crust and tender, slightly tacky crumb.

Recipe Notes
Breads & DoughsComponents & Basics
Yield1 loaf
Prep145 min
Cook30 min
Method400°F oven
DifficultyModerate
Main IngredientFlour

Ingredients

Dough

Cooking Stages

1

Start dough

Combine water, yeast, and sugar; rest about 5 minutes until foamy. Mix in 2 cups flour and olive oil, then salt and remaining flour.

2

Knead and rise

Knead about 7 minutes until smooth and springy. Oil the dough and let rise about 1 hour until doubled.

3

Shape and rise again

Shape into a tight loaf and place in a 9×4½-inch loaf pan. Cover and rise about 1 hour.

4

Bake with steam

Heat oven to 400°F. Place a shallow pan of water on the lowest rack shortly before baking. Slash loaf three times and bake about 30 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding.

Breads & Doughs · Italian

Roman-Style Focaccia

Long-fermented Roman-style focaccia with an airy chewy center, crisp golden exterior, olive oil, and flaky salt.

Recipe Notes Kept separately from Mariana’s seasoned family focaccia because the flour, fermentation, seasoning, and bake are materially different.
Breads & DoughsItalianComponents & Basics
Yield1 large 9×13 focaccia
Prep30 min + long proof
Cook30–35 min
Method425°F oven
DifficultyModerate
Main IngredientFlour

Ingredients

Dough

Cooking Stages

1

Mix

Stir flour, salt, yeast, and lukewarm water just until no dry streaks remain. Dough should be very sticky.

2

Cold proof

Coat with 2 tablespoons olive oil, cover, and refrigerate 12 hours.

3

Warm and pan proof

Let stand at room temperature 3 hours. Transfer to a parchment-lined 9×13 pan with 2 tablespoons oil; stretch gently and proof 3 hours more.

4

Dimple and bake

Heat oven to 425°F. Drizzle with remaining oil, dimple, add flaky salt and optional rosemary, and bake 30–35 minutes until crisp and golden.

Olive Oil Panettone Cake

Moist olive-oil orange cake with candied fruit and currants, layered with mascarpone-cream-cheese frosting.

Recipe Notes Stop mixing frosting once it holds stiff peaks so it does not curdle.
DessertsCakesHoliday
Yield12 servings
Prep35 min
Cook45–55 min
Method350°F oven
DifficultyModerate
Main IngredientCake

Ingredients

Cake

Mascarpone Frosting

Cooking Stages

1

Bake cake

Heat oven to 350°F. Prepare an 8-inch round pan. Mix dry ingredients separately; whisk oil and sugar, then eggs, yogurt, vanilla, zest, and juice. Fold in dry ingredients, candied peel, and currants. Bake 45–55 minutes until dark golden and a tester comes out clean.

2

Cool

Cool 10–15 minutes in the pan, then turn out and cool completely.

3

Make frosting

Beat cream cheese and powdered sugar smooth. Add mascarpone, vanilla, and salt. Add cream last and beat only until stiff peaks form.

4

Assemble

Split cake horizontally. Spread about one-third frosting between layers and use the rest outside. Garnish with candied peel if desired.

Pizza Dough

A versatile two-rise pizza dough for one large pizza or two smaller pizzas.

Recipe Notes Reusable quick pizza foundation; kept separately from the long-rise Neapolitan pizza-class dough.
Breads & DoughsPizzaComponents & Basics
Yield1 large or 2 small pizzas
Prep10 min + 2 hr rise
Cook8–10 min if baked
MethodDough / 500°F oven
DifficultyModerate
Main IngredientFlour

Ingredients

Dough

Cooking Stages

1

Bloom yeast

Stir yeast and honey into warm water and rest about 3 minutes until foamy.

2

Mix and knead

Mix flour and salt with the yeast mixture. Knead with a dough hook about 8 minutes; dough should pull from the sides but stay soft and slightly sticky.

3

Rise twice

Form into an oiled ball and rise about 1 hour. Punch down, divide if desired, and proof another hour.

4

Use

Roll or pat to desired thickness. For a basic pizza, bake at 500°F about 8–10 minutes until crisp and golden.

Glaze and finish

Brush chicken with mostarda and continue roasting until deeply golden and cooked through, about 15–20 minutes more. Rest before carving.

Vanilla Chocolate Chip Ice Cream

Classic vanilla CREAMi with mini chocolate chips, with Ninja’s official Full and Lite sweetener options in one recipe.

Full + LiteSwitch the entire recipe between versions below.
Frozen DessertsNinja CREAMiIce CreamFull + Lite
Yield1 CREAMi pint
Prep5–10 min
Freeze24 hr
MachineNinja CREAMi
DifficultyEasy
VersionsFull + Lite
Version

Full versionOfficial Ninja Test Kitchen full recipe.

Full Version Ingredients

Full Version Stages

1

Make the base

Microwave softened cream cheese for about 10 seconds. Stir in sugar and flavoring until smooth and frosting-like, about 60 seconds. Slowly whisk in the dairy until fully combined and the sugar dissolves.

2

Freeze

Pour into an empty CREAMi pint, cover, and freeze on a level surface for 24 hours.

3

Process

Install the frozen pint according to your machine instructions and run ICE CREAM.

4

Add mix-ins

Make a 1½-inch-wide hole down through the processed pint. Add ¼ cup mini chocolate chips and run MIX-IN.

5

Serve

Remove from the pint and serve immediately.

Lite Version Ingredients

Lite Version Stages

1

Make the Lite base

Microwave softened cream cheese for about 10 seconds. Stir in stevia, agave, and vanilla until smooth, then slowly whisk in heavy cream and milk until fully combined.

2

Freeze

Pour into an empty CREAMi pint, cover, and freeze on a level surface for 24 hours.

3

Process

Install the frozen pint according to your machine instructions and run LITE ICE CREAM.

4

Add mix-ins

Make a 1½-inch-wide hole down through the processed pint. Add ¼ cup mini chocolate chips and run MIX-IN.

5

Serve

Remove from the pint and serve immediately.

Options

Crumbly after processing: If you are not adding mix-ins, use RE-SPIN. Very cold freezers can make a pint look dry or crumbly on the first pass.

Mix-ins: Make a hole about 1½ inches wide through the processed portion, add mix-ins, then use MIX-IN.

Full vs. Lite: Use ICE CREAM for Full and LITE ICE CREAM for Lite. “Lite” describes the adapted CREAMi formula; it is not a nutrition claim.

Ninja note: Mini chocolate chips work best because the MIX-IN program does not break down hard ingredients.

Process top

Serve top

Process bottom

Serve

Soups & Stews · American

Texas-Style Meat Chili

Thick, meat-forward chili with coarse-ground beef, chile spices, beef stock, and no beans.

Not Yet Family-TestedScratch version inspired by Daniel’s memory of the meat-only Texas chili from Hard Times Cafe in the Washington, D.C. area.
Soups & StewsBeefComfort FoodFamily Dinner
Yield8 servings
Prep15 min
Cook45 min
MethodStovetop
DifficultyEasy
Main IngredientBeef

Ingredients

Meat Chili

Optional Toppings

Cooking Stages

1

Brown the beef

Brown the beef over medium-high heat, breaking it into small coarse crumbles. Work in batches if needed so it browns instead of steaming.

2

Cook the aromatics

Drain excess fat if needed. Add onion and cook 6–8 minutes until very soft. Add garlic and tomato paste and cook 1 minute.

3

Bloom the spices

Add chili powder, ancho powder, cumin, paprika, oregano, cayenne, salt, and pepper. Stir about 30 seconds until fragrant.

4

Simmer low and slow

Add beef stock and Worcestershire. Return all beef to the pot. Simmer uncovered on low 60–90 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and meat-forward rather than soupy.

5

Finish the texture

If it is still looser than you want, whisk 1 tablespoon masa harina with a little cool water and stir it in. Add more only if needed.

6

Balance and serve

Stir in vinegar, taste for salt and heat, and serve straight or with toppings. No beans.

Honey Ricotta Pancakes

Tender oat-flour pancakes with ricotta, honey, whipped egg whites, and an optional warm berry sauce.

Not Yet TestedGiadzy recipe by Kristin Cavallari
Breakfast & BrunchPancakesVegetarianGluten-FreeNot Yet Tested
Yield4 servings
Prep10 min
Cook15 min
MethodGriddle
DifficultyEasy
Main IngredientRicotta

Ingredients

Pancakes

Optional Warm Berry Sauce

Cooking Stages

1

Whip the whites

Beat the egg whites on high until stiff peaks form, about 2–3 minutes.

2

Mix the dry ingredients

Combine oat flour, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.

3

Mix the wet ingredients

Whisk almond milk, egg yolks, ricotta, honey, and vanilla. Fold in the whipped egg whites, then gently combine with the dry ingredients.

4

Cook the pancakes

Warm coconut oil in a skillet over medium heat. Portion batter and cook until bubbles appear, about 2–3 minutes; flip and cook about 3 minutes more.

5

Make the berry sauce, if using

Whisk arrowroot with 1 tablespoon water. Simmer lemon juice, berries, maple syrup, and remaining 3 tablespoons water for 3 minutes. Add arrowroot mixture and cook about 5 minutes until thick.

6

Serve

Serve warm with maple syrup, powdered sugar, berry sauce, or preferred toppings.

Mix the batter

Fluffy Lemon Buttermilk Pancakes

Light, fluffy buttermilk pancakes with lemon zest and whipped egg whites folded into the batter.

Not Yet TestedGiadzy recipe by Giada De Laurentiis
Breakfast & BrunchPancakesVegetarianNut-FreeNot Yet Tested
Yield4 servings
Prep15 min
Cook10 min
MethodGriddle
DifficultyBeginner
Main IngredientButtermilk

Ingredients

Pancakes

Cooking Stages

1

Heat the griddle

Preheat a griddle or large skillet over medium-low heat and lightly coat with vegetable oil.

2

Mix the dry ingredients

Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.

3

Prepare the wet ingredients

Combine buttermilk, vanilla, lemon zest, and egg yolks.

4

Whip the whites

Whisk egg whites to soft peaks, about 3 minutes.

5

Fold the batter

Gently stir the buttermilk mixture into the flour mixture until almost combined, then carefully fold in the egg whites.

6

Cook

Raise griddle to medium heat. Use about ½ cup batter per pancake. Cook about 2 minutes until bubbles form, flip, and cook about 1 minute more.

7

Serve

Keep warm in a low oven if needed, then serve with maple syrup and optional berries.

Mix the dry ingredients

Whisk oats, flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.

2

Mix the wet ingredients

Whisk buttermilk, vanilla, egg, egg white, honey, and vegetable oil.

3

Add wet to dry and whisk just until combined. Do not overmix. Let batter rest 3 minutes.

Breakfast & BrunchBreads & DoughsQuick BreadFamily-FriendlyNot Yet Tested
Yield1 loaf
Prep15 min
Cook55–65 min
Method350°F oven
DifficultyEasy
Main IngredientBanana

Ingredients

Banana Bread

Optional Add-In

Cooking Stages

1

Prepare

Heat oven to 350°F. Grease a 9×5-inch loaf pan and line with parchment if desired.

2

Mix the wet ingredients

Whisk mashed bananas, melted butter, brown sugar, eggs, and vanilla until evenly combined.

3

Mix the dry ingredients

Whisk flour, baking soda, salt, and optional cinnamon in a separate bowl.

4

Combine

Fold dry ingredients into banana mixture just until no dry flour remains. Do not overmix.

5

Add nuts, if using

Fold in chopped walnuts or pecans. For a nut-free loaf, simply leave them out.

6

Bake

Spread batter in loaf pan. Bake 55–65 minutes, until deep golden and a toothpick near the center comes out with a few moist crumbs but no wet batter.

7

Cool

Cool in pan about 15 minutes, then remove to a rack and cool further before slicing.

Options & Variations

Nut-Free: Leave out the walnuts or pecans. No other ingredient changes are needed.

With Nuts: Fold in ¾ cup chopped walnuts or pecans just before the batter goes into the pan.

Important: Any loaf made with nuts is not for Luciano’s daycare. For daycare use, prepare a separate nut-free loaf and avoid cross-contact with nuts.

Scale This Recipe

loaves

Scale by loaves. Keep ingredient ratios exact and bake each loaf in its own pan; baking time does not multiply.

Storage & Serving

Keep tightly wrapped at room temperature for about 2 days, then refrigerate for longer storage. Slices freeze well when individually wrapped.

For Luciano’s daycare: Only use the nut-free version and follow the daycare’s current no-nut rules.

Soups & Stews · Italian

Pappa al Pomodoro di "Luciana"

Tuscan tomato-and-bread soup made with stale bread, ripe tomatoes or passata, vegetable stock, basil, garlic, chile, and extra-virgin olive oil.

Not Yet TestedVacation recipe photographed in Italy: “Pappa al pomodoro di Luciana.”
Soups & StewsTuscanVegetarianVacation RecipeBread SoupNot Yet Tested
Yield6 servings
Prep15 min
Cook30 min + 1 hr rest
MethodStovetop
DifficultyEasy
Main IngredientTomatoes

Ingredients

Soup

Cooking Stages

1

Start the garlic

Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a pot. Sauté the chopped garlic and remove it as soon as it begins to change color.

2

Cook the tomato base

Add a pinch of hot chile pepper, the tomatoes or passata, plenty of basil leaves, salt, and black pepper. If using fresh tomatoes, crush them with a wooden spoon as they cook. Simmer 15 minutes.

3

Add stock and bread

Add the vegetable stock. Once it returns to a boil, add the stale bread cut into thin slices.

4

Cook the bread

Cook another 15 minutes, stirring often, until the bread softens deeply into the soup.

5

Rest

Remove from the heat and let the soup rest about 1 hour.

6

Mix and serve

Mix well so the bread is completely incorporated with the tomato mixture. Serve warm with 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil and fresh basil leaves.

Options & Variations

Tomatoes: The original page allows either 400 g fresh ripe tomatoes or 400 g passata.

Texture: The defining texture is thick and spoonable, with the stale bread fully mixed into the tomato base rather than left as separate chunks.

Scale This Recipe

servings

Roasted Garlic

Whole garlic roasted in a foil pouch until deeply golden, soft, sweet, and easy to squeeze from the skins.

Not Yet TestedDaniel’s Recipe Library kitchen basic.
Sauces & DipsComponents & BasicsVegetarianFamily-FriendlyNot Yet Tested
Yield1 garlic head
Prep5 min
Cook40–50 min
Method400°F oven
DifficultyEasy
Main IngredientGarlic

Ingredients

Roasted Garlic

Cooking Stages

1

Heat the oven

Heat oven to 400°F.

2

Expose the cloves

Slice about ¼ inch off the top of the garlic head so the tops of the cloves are exposed.

3

Oil the garlic

Set the garlic on a piece of foil. Drizzle the exposed cloves with olive oil and add a small pinch of salt if desired.

4

Wrap like a pouch

Bring the foil up and around the garlic to make a sealed ball or pouch. It does not need to be pressed tightly against the garlic; just seal it well enough to hold in the steam.

5

Roast

Roast 40–50 minutes, until the cloves are deeply golden, very soft, and easily pierced.

6

Cool and squeeze

Let cool until comfortable to handle, then squeeze the roasted cloves from their skins.

Options & Variations

Multiple heads: Wrap each head separately, or place several in a covered baking dish. The roasting time usually stays close to the same; judge by softness and deep golden color.

Scale This Recipe

heads
